findings.title: FBI FLASH on the ARTEX agentic intrusion framework
findings.summary: The FBI describes ARTEX as an open-source, LLM-driven multi-agent penetration-testing platform, written in Go, used since at least August 2026 to automate intrusion phases. The original repository was taken down on October 8, 2026 after reported abuse; copies, forks, and a commercial variant remain available. Researchers had identified more than 1,600 publicly exposed consoles as of early November 2026. Aggregate official figures include exfiltration of personal information from approximately 67,000 individuals and access to more than 2,250 downstream tenants in a cloud-backup compromise. This finding does not name those organizations.

audit.notes: Public official advisory only. No IOCs, payloads, or exploit steps retained. Victim organizations not named. Safe for a defensive public panel.

findings.title: UK NCSC: AI malware “highly likely” in ransomware against UK CNI (forecast)
findings.summary: The NCSC’s 3 November 2026 news release says UK critical national infrastructure should be braced for a ransomware attack involving AI-powered malware by 2028. The Annual Review states it is highly likely AI malware will be used in a ransomware attack on UK CNI, and that AI will mainly accelerate existing techniques rather than invent new attack vectors. This is an official judgment and forecast, not a report that such an attack has already occurred.

findings.title: Measurement study of MCP tool poisoning across agent frameworks
findings.summary: A paper (arXiv:2611.03555v2, submitted 2 November 2026, revised 9 November 2026, accepted at AISec ’26) reports a 9,720-cell test of MCP tool poisoning across 12 frameworks, 18 models, and 45 scenarios, with an overall attack success rate of 22.9%. The authors argue that MCP carries attacker-controlled tool descriptions, schema fields, and responses into model context without validation. This is a controlled measurement study, not a catalog of real-world breaches.
findings.sentinel_label: VERIFIED as research, not as a field-incident tally

findings.title: FBI FaceStealer FLASH: prerecorded replay, with a separate SI deepfake section
findings.summary: FBI FLASH AC-111226-MS (12 November 2026) describes a social-engineering scheme called FaceStealer that uses imposter video-meeting sites and a library of secretly recorded webcam videos of prior victims. The FBI says it has identified and seized more than 900 such videos and that the scheme has been used to steal more than $400 million in cryptocurrency over the past 18 months. Pages 1–3 and 6 describe prerecorded webcam replay. Page 4 has a dedicated section, “Emerging Use of SI to Generate Deepfake Videos,” so a generative-AI claim is present even though the scheme still overwhelmingly uses stolen genuine video. No victim names are recorded.
